items.title: Grok Imagine Image 2.0 now available on Vercel AI Gateway
items.excerpt: xAI's Grok Imagine Image 2.0 is now on Vercel AI Gateway as a preview: an image generation and editing model that plans typography and layout together and renders small text sharply. Typography-aware generation is exactly the failure mode that has kept most image models out of real layout work.

items.title: Using agents in Figma Design (and coming soon to FigJam and Slides)
items.excerpt: Figma's own walkthrough of working with agents inside Figma Design, with FigJam and Slides support flagged as next. It is the clearest official statement yet of how the agent is meant to sit inside an existing design file rather than replace it.

items.title: Teaching Your AI Web Design Some Actual Taste
items.excerpt: A practical writeup on why coding agents default to generic, templated UI, and what constraints and reference material actually move generated interfaces toward a distinct visual point of view.

items.title: Creating an AI Short Film (Full Workflow) | Runway
items.excerpt: Runway publishes an end-to-end production walkthrough for an AI short film, from idea through shot generation and edit. Useful as a concrete look at where generative video now fits in a real creative pipeline rather than a demo reel.

items.title: The AI shift most companies didn't see coming
items.excerpt: Microsoft Design on the organisational shift AI is forcing on product teams — what changes in how work is scoped and who does it. A design-org framing rather than a tool demo.

items.title: Autodesk is discontinuing Mudbox, its digital sculpting software
items.excerpt: Sales of the Academy Award-winning sculpting tool end this November. A long-standing part of many hard-surface and character pipelines is being retired, forcing teams onto ZBrush, Blender or Autodesk's newer generative 3D bets.

items.title: Bring Animated Maya Scenes To Blender & UE5 Instantly
items.excerpt: MableLink moves animated Maya scenes into Blender and Unreal Engine 5 in one click, with materials carried over and live re-sync on the Pro tier. Interchange friction is one of the least glamorous but most expensive costs in a 3D pipeline.

items.title: New CG software you may have missed: 9 August 2026
items.excerpt: CG Channel's weekly sweep of releases, covering FumeFX 7.6 for 3ds Max, Character Control Rig 0.3.1 for Blender and PFTrack 26.08 — a compact map of what actually shipped for 3D artists this week.

items.title: Normal F****** Sunglasses are the perfect answer to Meta's creepy smart glasses
items.excerpt: DuckDuckGo's sold-out anti-smart-glasses sunglasses are a product-design statement against camera-and-AI eyewear. A reminder that 'no sensors' is itself becoming a design position brands can ship.

items.title: Lightweight Box3D Physics Plug-In For Unreal Engine 5
items.excerpt: Antonio Lattanzio has released a free, open-source Box3D physics integration for Unreal Engine 5, giving prototypers a lighter alternative to Chaos for quick interactive tests.

items.title: Viture's new Pro XR glasses have the most useful party trick ever
items.excerpt: Viture Pro 2 lands at $300 as the company's thinnest AR glasses yet, with a mobile dock. Cheap wearable displays are quietly becoming a plausible second screen for design review and reference.

items.title: Vercel Sandbox now runs on Vercel Managed Images
items.excerpt: Vercel Sandbox now ships versioned, open-source base images with Node.js, Python and coding agents preinstalled, with Dockerfiles public. Relevant to any team running prompt-to-prototype agents in an isolated environment.

items.title: Three Clouds, Three Native Agents
items.excerpt: A side-by-side build of the same agent on three vendors' native stacks, showing how far the tool-use and orchestration models have diverged — useful context before committing a product team to one.

items.title: The Apple Watch redesign can't come soon enough
items.excerpt: Apple is reportedly preparing a smartwatch form-factor shake-up. A product-design read on why the current shape has run out of room as more of the interaction moves to voice and assistants.

items.title: Animating CSS border-image
items.excerpt: Border-image slices can run across an entire element border, and animating them produces effects that are hard to get any other way. A craft technique agents almost never reach for on their own.

items.title: Inside DNEG's Invisible Effects for Citadel Season 2
items.excerpt: DNEG's Daniel Baldwin breaks down fire, full-CG crashes and seamless camera handoffs for Citadel Season 2 — the invisible-effects craft that generative video still has no answer for.

items.title: This Is How You Advertise Frozen Shrimp
items.excerpt: A standout frozen-seafood spot made, in the creators' words, "pretty much entirely in Blender and After Effects with no use of AI" — an explicit no-AI credit is now itself a positioning choice in commercial work.

items.title: A Second Brain Your AI Agent Can Read: Obsidian + Claude
items.excerpt: Structuring notes as clean markdown so an agent can use them as working context — a lightweight pattern for giving design and product context to an assistant without a bespoke tool.

items.title: See Dexter Studios' VFX breakdown for The WONDERfools
items.excerpt: Dexter Studios' breakdown for the Korean superhero comedy covers teleportation, telekinesis and a giant inflatable onion — a look at how a mid-budget Korean feature builds effects shots.
